newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia '96 tin output dips 19.2 pct - industry.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia '96 tin output dips 19.2 pct - industry.

text.p: Malaysia's tin production dipped 19.2 percent to 5,174 tonnes last year, from 6,402 tonnes in 1995, the Malaysian Chamber of Mines (MCM) said on Thursday.
Average price of the metal fell 1.2 percent to 15.35 ringgit per kg through 1996, MCM president Abdul Sukor Shahar said in a statement released for the chamber's annual meeting.
The gross value of tin mined last year was also lower at 80 million ringgit, against 98 million ringgit in 1995, Andul Sukor said.
"Although tin's dominance in the Malaysian economy has waned somewhat over the years, it still contributes a fair share to the nation's foreign exchange," he said.
He said revenue from exports of refined tin dipped to 534 million ringgit in 1996 against 545 million ringgit in 1995.
Domestic tin consumption was also lower at 5,996 tonnes in 1996, compared with 6,350 tonnes the previous year, Abdul Sukor said.

The total value of minerals produced in Malaysia was 2.6 billion ringgit in 1996, up 7.5 percent from 2.4 billion in 1995. Other minerals mined in the country are copper, iron-ore, gold, silver, barite, kaolin, silica, limestone, granite, sand, gravel and coal.
